fields.summary: A/R and A/P Report Sorting - Story 1 - Reports open in QuickBooks name order
fields.description:
## Summary

Open all six A/R and A/P aging reports in customer or vendor name order, A to Z, compared the way QuickBooks compares names, with stable paging, so shops can reconcile them line by line against QuickBooks.

## Context

As an office or accounting user, I want each report to open in customer or vendor name order so that I can reconcile it against QuickBooks line by line.

Prerequisites: User must have 'Reports → Page Access' setting enabled.

Form factor: Desktop only by rule: these are detailed reports.

## Requirements

* S1-R1: A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z; A/P Summary opens with vendors in name order, A to Z.
* S1-R2: Name order compares names ignoring capitals, in plain character order: digits and punctuation compare as characters, so "10 Trucking" comes before "2 Trucking" and "A-1 Towing" before "a1 towing". Names that start with a punctuation mark follow the same order: "#1 Diesel", "-1 Diesel", "10 Trucking", "@Home Towing".
* S1-R3: Accented letters sort with their base letter: "Émile's" sorts among the E names (é è ê ë sort as e, á à â ä ã å as a, ç as c, ñ as n, ö ó ò ô õ ø as o, ü ú ù û as u, í ì î ï as i, ý ÿ as y, ß as ss, æ as ae, œ as oe, in both cases).
* S1-R4: Two names that compare equal are ordered by the plain lower-cased name, then by the customer or vendor itself, so the same two customers always come out in the same order on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV. For example, "Emile's Towing" comes before "Émile's Towing": the accent folds for the name order (S1-R3), so the two tie, and in the plain lower-cased name the unaccented letter comes first.
* S1-R5: A/R Detail and A/P Detail keep their aging buckets in this fixed order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current". Inside each bucket, rows open in customer or vendor name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4), ties by document number (S2-R4).
* S1-R6: A/R Collection groups by customer and A/P Unpaid Invoices by vendor, groups in name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4); inside each group, rows open oldest date first; rows on the same date, whatever the time of day they were created, go in document-number order (S2-R4).
* S1-R7: The column the report opened on is marked as sorted: the name column on the Summaries and Detail reports, the Date column on Collection and Unpaid Invoices.
* S1-R8: A/R Summary, A/P Summary, A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices show 30 customers or vendors at a time, and the next 30 load as the user scrolls down, as today. There are no page buttons. A/R Detail and A/P Detail show each bucket's first 100 lines, then load more as the user scrolls (S4-R4). Paging never repeats or skips a customer, vendor or row, in any sort.
* S1-N1: If the user lacks 'Reports → Page Access', the reports are not available, as today.
* S1-E1: A customer with no open documents on the as-of date does not appear, as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given A/R Summary with customers "2 Trucking", "10 Trucking", "a1 towing" and "A-1 Towing", when it opens, then the order is "10 Trucking", "2 Trucking", "A-1 Towing", "a1 towing" (S1-R1, S1-R2).
- [ ] Given a customer named "Émile's", when A/R Summary opens, then it sorts among the E names, and every accented letter in S1-R3 sorts with its base letter in both cases (S1-R3).
- [ ] Given two customers whose names compare equal, when the report, its PDF and its CSV are produced, then the two come out in the same order in all three; "Emile's Towing" comes before "Émile's Towing" (S1-R4).
- [ ] Given A/R Detail or A/P Detail, when it opens, then the buckets read "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current" in that order, and rows inside each bucket are in name order, ties by document number (S1-R5).
- [ ] Given A/R Collection or A/P Unpaid Invoices, when it opens, then groups are in name order and rows inside each group are oldest date first, ties by document number, and the Date column is marked sorted; on the other four the name column is marked sorted (S1-R6, S1-R7).
- [ ] Given a report with more than 30 customers, vendors or rows, when the user scrolls through it, the next 30 loading as they scroll (no page buttons), in any sort (with and without Past due ranges ticked), then no customer, vendor or row repeats or is skipped (S1-R8).
- [ ] Given a user without 'Reports → Page Access', then the reports are not available (S1-N1); given a customer with nothing open on the as-of date, then it is not listed (S1-E1).

## UI/UX

Design: page 1 (Opening order and header sorting)

[A/R and A/P Report Sorting design canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4)

## PRD

[A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter, Story 1](https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=947650561)

# QA Handoff — SV-11531 Story 1 — reports open in QuickBooks name order

**QA env:** https://sv11315.qa.shopview.com · **PR:** https://github.com/ShopView/shopview/pull/4262 (branch `SV-11315-ar-ap-aging-reports`, head `8e35ee0d02`)
**Screens:** all six — `/reports/ar-aging-summary`, `/reports/ar-aging-detail`, `/reports/ar-aging-collection`, `/reports/ap-aging-summary`, `/reports/ap-aging-detail`, `/reports/ap-unpaid-invoices`
**Shared notes** (roles, test data, known mismatches): https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11315?focusedCommentId=80616
**Video:** `sv-11531-opening-order-v2.mp4` (also covers SV-11441 and SV-12140)

---

## What changed

Every report has a fixed opening order. Names sort the way QuickBooks sorts them. Buckets, groups and documents come out in the same order on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV. The bucket a document lands in and its Past Due are counted in calendar days at the location.

## QA Checklist (do these)

### Name order — Summaries \[S1-R1–S1-R4\]

- [ ] Customers "10 Trucking", "2 Trucking", "A-1 Towing", "a1 towing", "Émile's", "Emile's Towing", "Émile's Towing", "Øster", "Ozone" with one open invoice each. Open A/R Aging Summary with only these ticked in the Customer filter → order is: 10 Trucking, 2 Trucking, A-1 Towing, a1 towing, Emile's Towing, Émile's, Émile's Towing, Øster, Ozone.
- [ ] "Emile's Towing" comes before "Émile's Towing". Accented names sit among the plain E and O names.
- [ ] Names starting with punctuation: "#1 Diesel", "-1 Diesel", "10 Trucking", "@Home Towing" in exactly that order (see SV-12140).
- [ ] The Customer header shows the sort arrow on open \[S1-R7\].
- [ ] Same on A/P Aging Summary with vendors (Vendor header marked).

### Detail reports — buckets \[S1-R5, S1-R5a\]

* \[ \] A/R Detail and A/P Detail list five buckets in this order under any sort: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current". Each shows its count "(N)". All start closed.
* \[ \] Open a bucket → lines in customer (A/R) or vendor (A/P) name order; one customer's documents in document-number order (S3-99, S3-100, S3-101). "Customer Full Name" / "Vendor Name" header marked.
* \[ \] A document lands in a bucket by calendar days at the location: due on or after the as-of date → "Current"; due 1–30 days before → "1-30 days past due"; and so on.
* \[ \] A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit dated **on** the as-of date is in "Current"; one dated the day before is in "1-30 days past due" (full steps in SV-11441).
* \[ \] A/R invoices not yet due are in "Current". Where Past Due shows (A/P Detail), a bill due in 10 days reads "-10".

### Collection and Unpaid — groups \[S1-R6, S1-R7\]

- [ ] A/R Collection groups by customer, A/P Unpaid by vendor, groups in name order. Inside a group, documents oldest date first. The Date header is marked.
- [ ] Several documents on the same date go in document-number order (S3-14690, S3-14691, …), whatever time they were created (see SV-12138).
- [ ] A/R Collection lists only overdue invoices (Past Due 1 or more in calendar days) plus every unused credit memo and deposit. An invoice due today is not listed; one due yesterday is, with Past Due 1.

### Paging \[S1-R8\]

- [ ] Summaries, A/R Collection, A/P Unpaid: 30 customers or vendors show; scroll to the bottom → the next 30 load. No page buttons. Compare names around rows 30/31: nothing repeats or is skipped. Repeat after sorting by Total and with a Past due range ticked.
- [ ] Detail: an open bucket shows its first 100 lines; scroll to its end → the next 100, until the count is reached. Unique numbers = "(N)". (New on A/R Detail.)
- [ ] A/R Collection / A/P Unpaid: an open customer or vendor with more than 100 documents shows 100, then 100 more each time you scroll to its end. Its "(N)", its "Total for <name>" row, the Totals row and both exports cover every document.

### Access and empty \[S1-N1, S1-E1\]

- [ ] A user without Reports → Page Access does not see the reports.
- [ ] A customer or vendor with nothing open on the as-of date is not listed.

## Known mismatches (not bugs)

* Bills not yet due show negative Past Due ("-10" for a bill due in 10 days). Product decision, see the shared notes (https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11315?focusedCommentId=80616).
* Inside a group over 100 documents, the browser's Find only finds documents already drawn \[S1-R8\].

## What is NOT impacted

- [ ] Other reports (Sales By Customer, Inventory Value, Work In Progress, …).
- [ ] Work order, part sale, delivery and vendor return pages (only opened from the reports).

## Dev verification

* \[x\] Tests: `ReportNameOrderSqlTest`, `AgingSqlTest` (name key, number key, calendar-day buckets at every boundary, `testDaysBeforeTheAsOfDayAreCalendarDays`), `AgingLocalDaySqlTest`, `AgingTodayAgedAtEndOfDayTest`, `DbalArAgingQueryRepositoryTest`, `DbalArAgingDetailTest`, `DbalApAgingDetailTest`, `DbalArAgingCollectionTest`, `DbalApUnpaidInvoicesTest`, `useAgingGroupRowWindows.spec.ts`, `useAgingBucketPages.spec.ts`. MySQL 8.0.42 proof `api/tools/sql/aging-name-order-check.sql` = its expected file.
* \[x\] Test ids: `header_<code>_<column>` (sort arrow), `aging_detail_report_row_<bucket>_cell_bucket`, `row_ardet_load_more_<bucket>`, `row_arcol_load_more_<customerId>`, `row_apunp_load_more_<vendorId>`.
* \[x\] Review rounds: phases 1–5 and the as-of / Past Due fix (asof-r2), all approved.
* \[x\] Walks: p5walk 13/13; Expand all on the largest local groups 0.63–0.77 s; the video above is being re-recorded on the current build.

fields.summary: A/R and A/P Report Sorting - Story 2 - Sort by clicking any column header
fields.description:
## Summary

Make every column on the six reports sortable from its header, with the first click giving the useful order for the data type, so users can work the aging in priority order.

## Context

As a user working the aging, I want to sort by any column in one click so that I can work the list in priority order.

Prerequisites: User must have 'Reports → Page Access' setting enabled.

Form factor: Desktop only by rule: detailed reports.

## Requirements

* S2-R1: Every column on all six reports sorts when its header is clicked, except A/P Unpaid Invoices' Vendor Name column (S2-N1). The columns are: • A/R Summary and A/P Summary: the name column, Location (when shown), Current, 1-30 Days, 31-60 Days, 61-90 Days, 91 And Over, Total. • A/R Detail: Date, Location (when shown), Transaction Type, ID, Customer Full Name, Due Date, Amount, Open Balance. • A/R Collection: Date, Location (when shown), Transaction Type, ID, Due Date, Past Due, Amount, Open Balance. • A/P Detail and A/P Unpaid Invoices: Date, Location (when shown), Transaction Type, No., Vendor Name, Due Date, Past Due, Amount, Open Balance.
* S2-R2: The first click gives the useful order for the kind of data: text (names, Location, Transaction Type) A to Z; money columns largest first; dates oldest first; Past Due largest first; ID and No. smallest number first (S2-R4). The second click reverses it. The third click repeats the first; there is no unsorted state.
* S2-R3: A header that is already the sorted column reverses on its first click.
* S2-R4: ID and No. sort by number value: S1-99 before S1-100 before S1-101. The first click puts the smallest number first and the second click the largest first. The same number-aware order breaks ties in every sort, always smallest document number first: reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only, so tied rows keep that order in both directions. A date column compares the day only, never the time of day, so two rows on the same date are a tie.
* S2-R4a: Column headings are in Title Case on all six reports, on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV, as on the other reports (Sales By Customer, Inventory Value, Parts Velocity): the A/R reports read "Transaction Type", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Past Due" and "Open Balance", the same as the A/P reports.
* S2-R5: On the grouped reports, a header click sorts the rows inside each group; the groups themselves never move (S1-R5, S1-R6).
* S2-R6: A blank value (for example a vendor credit on A/P Unpaid Invoices, which has no due date and no Past Due) sorts to the bottom of its group in both directions. On A/P Detail a vendor credit shows its own date as its due date, as today, so it is not blank there.
* S2-R7: The sort is kept while the user stays on the report: changing the as-of date, loading more rows by scrolling, and changing the customer, vendor, Past due or Location filter keep it.
* S2-R8: The sort is not remembered between visits: opening the report again starts from Story 1's order.
* S2-R9: Re-sorting never changes which groups are expanded or collapsed (Story 4).
* S2-N1: On A/P Unpaid Invoices, the Vendor Name header is not clickable, because every group holds a single vendor and sorting by it could never change the order.
* S2-E1: A column where every row has the same value (for example Location when each customer has one location) shows no visible change; the tie-break (S2-R4) still applies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given any of the six reports, when the user clicks each header listed in S2-R1, then the rows re-sort by that column; on A/P Unpaid Invoices the Vendor Name header is not clickable (S2-R1, S2-N1).
- [ ] Given an unsorted text column (name, Location, Transaction Type), when clicked once, then A to Z; a money column, largest first; a date column, oldest first; Past Due, largest first; a second click reverses; a third click repeats the first (S2-R2).
- [ ] Given the column the report opened on, when its header is clicked, then it reverses on that first click (S2-R3).
- [ ] Given documents S1-99, S1-100 and S1-101, when ID or No. is clicked once, then they read S1-99, S1-100, S1-101, and a second click reads S1-101, S1-100, S1-99; two rows tied on the sorted column stay smallest document number first in both directions (S2-R4). The A/R headings read "Transaction Type", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Past Due" and "Open Balance", in Title Case like the A/P reports, on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV (S2-R4a).
- [ ] Given a grouped report, when any header is clicked, then rows re-sort inside each group and the groups do not move, and expanded groups stay expanded (S2-R5, S2-R9).
- [ ] Given A/P Unpaid Invoices with a vendor credit, when Due Date or Past Due is sorted either way, then the credit sits at the bottom of its vendor group (S2-R6).
- [ ] Given a sorted report, when the user changes the as-of date, scrolls to load more rows, or changes the customer or vendor, Past due or Location filter, then the sort is kept; when the user opens the report again from the Reports menu, then it opens in Story 1's order (S2-R7, S2-R8).

## UI/UX

Design: page 1 (Opening order and header sorting)

[A/R and A/P Report Sorting design canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4)

## PRD

[A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter, Story 2](https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=947650561)

# QA Handoff — SV-11532 Story 2 — sort by clicking any column header

**QA env:** https://sv11315.qa.shopview.com · **PR:** https://github.com/ShopView/shopview/pull/4262 (branch `SV-11315-ar-ap-aging-reports`, head `8e35ee0d02`)
**Screens:** all six aging reports
**Shared notes** (roles, test data, known mismatches): https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11315?focusedCommentId=80616
**Video:** `sv-11532-sorting.mp4` (also covers SV-12135). Recorded before two small fixes: Past Due in calendar days and the sorted column's arrow strength on hover (see the shared notes (https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-11315?focusedCommentId=80616)).

---

## What changed

Every header sorts. The first click gives the useful order for that kind of data, the second reverses it. Ties always keep the smallest document number first. Dates are plain dates, credits are named, and a Location sort falls back when the Location column hides.

## QA Checklist (do these)

### Headers and first click \[S2-R1, S2-R2, S2-R3, S2-R4a\]

- [ ] Headings (Title Case, screen, PDF and CSV):
- [ ] ↳ Summaries: Customer / Vendor, Location (when shown), Current, 1-30 Days, 31-60 Days, 61-90 Days, 91 And Over, Total.
- [ ] ↳ A/R Detail: Date, Location, Transaction Type, ID, Customer Full Name, Due Date, Amount, Open Balance (no Past Due).
- [ ] ↳ A/R Collection: Date, Location, Transaction Type, ID, Due Date, Past Due, Amount, Open Balance.
- [ ] ↳ A/P Detail and A/P Unpaid: Date, Location, Transaction Type, No., Vendor Name, Due Date, Past Due, Amount, Open Balance.
- [ ] First click: text (names, Location, Transaction Type) A to Z; money largest first; dates oldest first; Past Due largest first; ID / No. smallest number first. Second click reverses; third repeats. No unsorted state.
- [ ] The column the report opened on reverses on its first click \[S2-R3\].
- [ ] A/P Unpaid: the Vendor Name header is not clickable (it is the group). On A/P Detail it is.
- [ ] The sorted header shows its arrow at full strength, also while you hover or focus it. Hovering another header shows a faint arrow hint.
- [ ] On the four grouped reports, hovering or clicking the Expand all chevron (in the Date heading) never lights Date's arrow and never sorts \[S4-R3\].

### Inside groups and buckets \[S2-R9, S4-R8\]

* \[ \] A/R Collection / A/P Unpaid: a sort reorders documents **inside** each customer or vendor; the groups never move; open groups stay open.
* \[ \] Detail: a sort reorders lines inside each bucket; buckets never move; open buckets stay open and start again at their first 100 lines.

### Ties and dates \[S2-R4, S1-R6\]

- [ ] Rows with the same value keep the smallest document number first, in both directions.
- [ ] Date compares the day only: same-day rows stay in document-number order both ways (SV-12138).
- [ ] Date and Due Date read like "Nov 5, 2026" on every row, including today, yesterday and 2 days ago — never "Today", "Yesterday" or "2 days ago" \[S2-R1a\]. The date is the location's day: a document created late in the evening shows that evening's date.

### Past Due and blanks \[S2-R6\]

- [ ] Past Due is left-aligned. First click: largest first. Values are calendar days at the location; bills not yet due are negative ("-10" for a bill due in 10 days) and sort below 0.
- [ ] A/P Unpaid vendor credit: Due Date and Past Due read "—" and stay at the bottom of their group in both directions.
- [ ] A/P Detail vendor credit: Due Date = its own date (not "—"), so it sorts among the bills.

### Credit names \[S2-R1b\]

- [ ] Transaction Type reads "Invoice", "Credit Memo" or "Deposit" on A/R, "Invoice" or "Vendor Credit" on A/P. Never "Credit".
- [ ] Click Transaction Type → A to Z by these names: A/R Credit Memo → Deposit → Invoice; A/P Invoice → Vendor Credit. Second click reverses; same-type rows keep the smallest number first.

### Sort kept, not remembered \[S2-R7, S2-R8\]

- [ ] Sort by Open Balance (or Total), then change As of, Customer / Vendor, Past due and Location → the sort stays. Scroll to load more → still sorted.
- [ ] Leave the report and open it again from the Reports menu → back to the opening order.
- [ ] Switch location (top right) while on a report → filters and rows stay, the sort returns to the opening order, groups collapse.

### Location sort falls back when the column hides \[S2-R7a\]

- [ ] With 2+ locations, sort by Location (A to Z), then tick a single location → the Location column hides and the sort returns to the opening order, with that header marked (the name column on the Summaries and Detail; Date, oldest first, on A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid). Rows, page address and exports follow.
- [ ] Tick a second location again → the column returns; the sort stays on the opening order.
- [ ] A new As of that leaves only one location in the list → the same fallback.
- [ ] Sorted by any other column, narrowing to one location keeps that sort.
- [ ] Every customer at one location: sorting by Location shows no visible change \[S2-E1\].

## Known mismatches (not bugs)

* Three date formats: screen "Nov 4, 2026", PDF "Nov 04 2026", CSV "2026-11-04" (Product decision).
* PRD S2-R7a mentions only narrowing the filter; the fallback happens whenever the Location column hides (Product agreed, wording fix pending).
* Bills not yet due show negative Past Due (Product decision).

## What is NOT impacted

- [ ] Other reports' sorting. The only shared change is the header arrow hint style, also used by Technician Utilization, Sales By Customer and Sales By Representative: there the sorted arrow keeps full strength on hover and the faint hint still shows on other headers.
- [ ] Work order, part sale, delivery and vendor return pages.

## Dev verification

* \[x\] Tests: `ReportSortableHeaderRow.spec.ts`, `ReportSortKeyTest`, `ReportPaginatorOrderByTest`, `AgingDetailSqlTest`, `AgingGroupedSqlTest`, `DbalArAgingCollectionTest` / `DbalApAgingDetailTest::testTransactionTypeSortsByItsNamesWithTiesByNumberBothWays`, `agingCellFormat.spec.ts` (plain dates, location time zone), `useAgingLocationSortFallback.spec.ts` and the six report specs.
* \[x\] Test ids: `header_<code>_<column>`, `button_<code>_toggle_all`, `tooltip_<code>_toggle_all`.
* \[x\] Review rounds: phases 1–5, design fixes (design-r2), sort caret (caret-r2), as-of / Past Due (asof-r2), all approved. Caret checked in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

    * \[x\] Walks: SV-12135 step check — every header both ways on all six reports — all pass; video 18/18 checks.

fields.summary: A/R and A/P Report Sorting - Story 3 - Export to PDF and CSV
fields.description:
## Summary

Give each of the six reports the native Export menu with PDF and CSV, exactly matching the rows, filters and sort on screen; A/P gains a PDF for the first time and A/R's Print button is replaced.

## Context

As a user, I want to download any of the six reports as a PDF or a CSV in the order on screen so that I can file, print, share or analyze it outside ShopView.

Prerequisites: User must have 'Reports → Page Access' setting enabled.

Form factor: Desktop only by rule: detailed reports.

## Requirements

* S3-R1: Each of the six reports has the native report Export menu (the ⋯ button at the right of the title row, labelled "Export report") with "Download (PDF)" and "Download (CSV)". A/R's former Print button is replaced by this menu. The A/P reports gain a PDF.
* S3-R2: The PDF downloads as a file.
* S3-R3: The PDF and the CSV contain exactly the rows on screen for the chosen as-of date, customer or vendor and locations, in the on-screen sort, including a sort changed after an earlier export, without refreshing the page.
* S3-R4: Each export states the as-of date the user picked: the PDF "As of Oct 15, 2026", the CSV "As of: Oct 15, 2026" (format: three-letter month, day, four-digit year).
* S3-R5: Each export states the locations under the as-of line: "Locations: All locations" when every location is ticked, otherwise "Locations: " followed by the ticked locations' names in the Location menu's order (A to Z), separated by a comma and a space, for example "Locations: Main Shop, North Bay". Under it, only when set: "Past due: " and the ticked ranges in menu order (for example "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days"), then, for one ticked customer or vendor, "Customer: " or "Vendor: " and the name, and for several, "Customers: " or "Vendors: " and the names in the order they were ticked.
* S3-R6: The Location column appears in the export under the same rule as on screen (Story 6).
* S3-R7: The A/R and A/P Summary PDF and CSV head the last bucket column "91 And Over", exactly as the screen shows it; in the PDF the heading stays on one line.
* S3-R8: The CSV starts with the lines of S3-R5, each in its own row, in this order: As of, Locations, then Past due and the customer or vendor line only when set. The column heading row follows directly, then one flat table: one row per customer or vendor (Summaries) or per document (Detail, Collection, Unpaid Invoices), with the aging bucket, customer or vendor in its own column; no group header or subtotal rows; one Totals row at the bottom. Money is a plain number with two decimals, and an empty bucket is a blank cell; dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
* S3-R8b: The CSV column headings are the on-screen headings, letter for letter (S2-R4a): "Customer Full Name" on A/R Detail, "Customer" on A/R Collection, "Vendor Name" on the A/P reports. The bucket column on A/R Detail and A/P Detail is headed "Aging Bucket", and its values are the bucket names shown on screen.
* S3-R8a: On A/R Collection, every CSV row also carries the customer's "Phone" and, for users with 'View and Manage AP/AR Data', "Credit term", in columns right after "Customer"; the PDF prints them on each customer's line (Story 9).
* S3-R9: The row count for the export limits is the number of customer or vendor rows (Summaries) or document rows (the other four), not counting headers, subtotals or the Totals row.
* S3-R10: A successful export shows the native "Success" message, "Data exported successfully." An export with no rows downloads nothing and shows the native warning "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results".
* S3-N1: Over 2,000 rows, the PDF is refused before anything is generated: no download, and the message "This report is too large for PDF. Export it as CSV, or narrow the filters, then try again." Exactly 2,000 rows is allowed.
* S3-N2: Over 50,000 rows, the CSV is refused: no download, and the message "This report is too large to export. Choose an earlier as-of date, then try again." Exactly 50,000 rows is allowed.
* S3-N3: A refused export shows exactly one message (S3-N1 or S3-N2), never a second generic error.
* Error handling: If an export fails for any other reason (a server error or a lost connection), nothing downloads and one error message shows: "We couldn't export this report. Please try again." This message is on these six reports only; the other reports keep theirs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given any of the six reports, when the user opens the ⋯ menu right of the title, then it offers "Download (PDF)" and "Download (CSV)", and A/R no longer has a Print button (S3-R1).
- [ ] Given a report sorted and filtered on screen (including a sort changed after an earlier export), when the user downloads the PDF and the CSV, then both hold exactly the on-screen rows in the on-screen order, and the PDF downloads as a file (S3-R2, S3-R3).
- [ ] Given as-of date Oct 15, 2026, one location ticked, the 31-60 and 91+ day ranges ticked and two customers ticked, then the PDF reads "As of Oct 15, 2026", the CSV "As of: Oct 15, 2026", then "Locations: <name>" (two ticked locations read in Location menu order, A to Z, for example "Locations: Main Shop, North Bay"), "Past due: 31-60 days, 91+ days" and "Customers: <first>, <second>" in the order ticked; with one customer it reads "Customer: <name>"; the Past due and Customer lines appear only when set (S3-R4, S3-R5).
- [ ] Given A/R or A/P Summary, then the PDF and CSV head the last bucket "91 And Over", on one line in the PDF (S3-R7).
- [ ] Given any CSV, then it starts with the As of and Locations lines (and the Past due and customer or vendor lines when set), one per row, directly above the column headings; the headings match the screen letter for letter and the bucket column is "Aging Bucket"; then it is one flat table with the bucket, customer or vendor in its own column, no group or subtotal rows, one Totals row, money as plain two-decimal numbers, empty buckets blank, dates YYYY-MM-DD; on A/R Collection, Phone and (with 'View and Manage AP/AR Data') Credit term follow Customer (S3-R5, S3-R8, S3-R8a, S3-R8b).
- [ ] Given 2,001 rows, when PDF is chosen, then nothing downloads and exactly one message shows: "This report is too large for PDF. Export it as CSV, or narrow the filters, then try again."; 2,000 rows downloads (S3-N1, S3-N3, S3-R9).
- [ ] Given 50,001 rows, when CSV is chosen, then nothing downloads and exactly one message shows: "This report is too large to export. Choose an earlier as-of date, then try again."; 50,000 rows downloads (S3-N2, S3-N3).
- [ ] Given a successful export, then "Success", "Data exported successfully." shows; given no rows, then "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results" and nothing downloads; given a server error or lost connection, then "We couldn't export this report. Please try again." shows once (S3-R10, Error Handling).

## Summary

On the four grouped reports, add a Collapse all / Expand all chevron in the top-left header cell and keep the group row in view pinned under the column headings while scrolling.

## Context

As a user reading a grouped report, I want to open or close every group at once and always see which group I'm scrolling through so that I don't lose my place.

Prerequisites: The report is a grouped report: A/R Detail, A/R Collection, A/P Detail or A/P Unpaid Invoices.

Form factor: Desktop only by rule: detailed reports.

## Requirements

* S4-R1: The table's top-left header cell holds one chevron button. While any group is expanded it points down, its tooltip (above the button) reads "Collapse all", and a click collapses every group. When every group is collapsed it points right, its tooltip reads "Expand all", and a click expands every group.
* S4-R2: After Expand all, groups that arrive later as the user scrolls also arrive expanded.
* S4-R3: Clicking the button never sorts the column under it.
* S4-R4: On A/R Detail and A/P Detail, expanding a bucket (by hand or with Expand all) shows its first 100 lines, then loads more as the user scrolls. This is as today on A/P Detail and new on A/R Detail, which today shows a whole bucket at once.
* S4-R5: Each group's own expand toggle uses the same chevron: pointing down when open, right when closed. Behavior is unchanged.
* S4-R6: While the user scrolls through an expanded group, that group's row (the bucket label, customer or vendor) stays pinned just under the column headings. Only one group row is held at a time: when the next group's row reaches it, the next row pushes it up and off and takes its place. Scrolling back reverses this.
* S4-R7: When the table scrolls sideways, each group row's label stays visible at the left.
* S4-R8: Re-sorting and paging keep every group's expanded or collapsed state.
* S4-R9: Expanded state is not remembered between visits.
* S4-N1: Changing the as-of date, the customer or vendor filter, the Past due filter or the Location filter collapses every group, as changing the date or filter does today.
* S4-N2: A/R Summary and A/P Summary have no groups, so they have no Collapse all button.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a grouped report with any group open, when the user hovers the top-left chevron, then it points down with tooltip "Collapse all" above it, and a click collapses every group without sorting the column; with every group closed it points right, reads "Expand all", and a click expands every group (S4-R1, S4-R3).
- [ ] Given Expand all, when more groups load while scrolling, then they arrive expanded; on A/R Detail and A/P Detail each bucket shows its first 100 lines and loads more on scroll (S4-R2, S4-R4).
- [ ] Given each group's own toggle, then it uses the same chevron, down when open and right when closed (S4-R5).
- [ ] Given an expanded group taller than the screen, when the user scrolls, then its group row stays pinned under the headings until the next group row pushes it off; scrolling back reverses it; when the table scrolls sideways, the label stays visible at the left (S4-R6, S4-R7).
- [ ] Given open groups, when the user re-sorts or pages, then they stay open; when the user changes the as-of date, customer or vendor, Past due or Location, then every group collapses; when the user reopens the report, then nothing is remembered (S4-R8, S4-R9, S4-N1).
- [ ] Given A/R Summary or A/P Summary, then there is no Collapse all button (S4-N2).

## UI/UX

Design: page 3 (Collapse all and pinned group rows)

[A/R and A/P Report Sorting design canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4)

---

## What changed

One chevron opens or closes every group. The group you scroll through stays pinned under the headings. Group rows follow the design: a closed group shows its totals on its own row; an open group ends with a "Total for <name>" row. Detail buckets load 100 lines at a time, and so do very large customers or vendors on A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid.

## QA Checklist (do these)

### Group rows (design)

* \[ \] Closed group: chevron (pointing right) in the first cell, then the bold name and bold count, e.g. "**91 or more days past due (12)**" or "**Acme Towing (5)**"; a bold "Total" in the column before Amount; bold Amount and Open Balance.
* \[ \] Open group: the group row shows only the chevron (pointing down) and the name with its count. After the last line: "Total for 91 or more days past due" (or "Total for Acme Towing") with bold Amount and Open Balance.
* \[ \] The "Total for" amounts equal the closed row's amounts.
* \[ \] Group rows are white (no grey band); document lines are not indented.

### Expand all / Collapse all \[S4-R1, S4-R2, S4-R3, S4-R5\]

- [ ] The header chevron sits in the Date heading, before "Date". With every group closed it points right and its tooltip (above) reads "Expand all"; with any group open it points down and reads "Collapse all".
- [ ] Clicking it never sorts the Date column, and never lights Date's sort arrow (hover or focus).
- [ ] Expand all on A/R Collection, then scroll until the next 30 customers load → they arrive open.
- [ ] Each group's own chevron toggles that group only.
- [ ] Detail: Expand all opens every bucket that has lines. An empty bucket reads "(0)" and its chevron is greyed.

### 100 lines at a time \[S4-R4, S1-R8\]

- [ ] Detail: an open bucket shows its first 100 lines; scroll to its end → a small spinner row, then the next 100, until "(N)" is reached. No line repeats or is skipped. The "Total for" row appears after the last line.
- [ ] A/R Collection / A/P Unpaid: a customer or vendor with more than 100 documents draws 100, then 100 more each time you scroll to its end. Its "(N)" and amounts, the Totals row and both exports cover every document; its "Total for" row shows once the last document is drawn.
- [ ] Re-sort, or close and reopen → the group starts again at its first 100.
- [ ] Expand all on the largest vendor (A/P Unpaid) opens in about a second; scrolling stays smooth.

### Pinned group row \[S4-R6\]

- [ ] Scroll through a long open group → its row (name and count; on A/R Collection also Phone and Credit term) stays pinned under the headings. The next group's row pushes it up and takes its place. Scrolling back reverses it.
- [ ] The pinned row stays while the next 100 load.

### Sideways scroll \[S4-R7\]

* \[ \] Make the window narrower than about 1440 px (or zoom in) and scroll the table sideways: a **closed** group's bold name and count stay visible at the left, on the row's own colour (light, dark, hover).
* \[ \] On A/R Collection, Phone and Credit term slide under the name; the name stays readable.
* \[ \] Check 1024 px and 375 px on all four reports.

### Kept and reset \[S4-R8, S4-R9, S4-N1\]

- [ ] Re-sorting or scrolling keeps every group open or closed as it was.
- [ ] Changing As of, Customer / Vendor, Past due or Location collapses every group.
- [ ] Leave and come back → all closed.

### Bucket errors (Detail) \[Story 4 Error Handling\]

* \[ \] DevTools → Network request blocking `*/buckets/*/rows*`, expand a bucket → in place of its lines: "Something went wrong loading this bucket. Collapse and expand it to try again." Other buckets are unaffected.
* \[ \] Remove the block, collapse and expand that bucket → its lines load. While it reads again you see the loading row, not the old error.
* \[ \] Open a bucket with more than 100 lines, then block the pattern and scroll to its end → the lines already shown stay, and the bucket ends with "Not every line loaded. Collapse and expand this bucket to try again."
* \[ \] Same on A/P Detail.

## Known mismatches (not bugs)

* **SR-2 (follow-up):** on a sideways scroll the group's chevron scrolls away with the table; only the name and count stay. Scroll back left to use it.
* At 375 px a closed group's Amount covers the end of a long name (kept; no money value is cut).
* A/R Detail's columns shift about 34 px sideways when you click Expand all.
* A failing bucket (server error) also raises the app-wide "Ooooops! An error occurred" toast next to the bucket message.
* Inside a group over 100 documents, the browser's Find only finds documents already drawn, and the scrollbar grows as you scroll (PRD S1-R8).

## What is NOT impacted

- [ ] A/R Summary and A/P Summary (no groups).
- [ ] Other reports' group rows (the pinned-row and expansion pieces are opt-in).

## Dev verification

* \[x\] Tests: `useReportGroupExpansion.spec.ts`, `ReportPinnedGroupRow.spec.ts`, `useReportPinnedGroup.spec.ts`, `AgingDocumentRows.spec.ts`, `useAgingGroupRowWindows.spec.ts`, `useAgingBucketPages.spec.ts` (later page fails → lines kept + hint; failed first page → message; re-read shows loading), `agingColumns.spec.ts` (group row layout), the four report specs (bucket error text exact).

## Summary

Give all six reports the native filter row: As of, Customer (A/R) or Vendor (A/P), Past due and Location, with totals, paging, sort, exports and drill-down following every filter; the reports stay organization-wide.

## Context

As a manager of a multi-location shop, I want to narrow the aging to chosen locations so that I can follow up on my own branch.

Prerequisites: User must have 'Reports → Page Access' setting enabled.

Form factor: Desktop only by rule: detailed reports.

## Requirements

* S5-R1: Each report's filter row is the native report filter row of the newer reports (Inventory Value, Sales By Customer), in this order on all six reports: the date chip ("As of: 10/15/2026"), the customer chip on the A/R reports or the vendor chip on the A/P reports, the Past due chip, then the Location chip.
* S5-R2: The Location chip and its open menu are the native ones, exactly as on Sales By Customer, Inventory Value and Work In Progress: label "Location" with the location pin icon; the menu shows a "Select all" row, a "{N} selected" count, the locations with the ticked ones first, a search box with the placeholder "Search locations" once there are more than 8 locations, and "Clear selection".
* S5-R3: The list offers every location at which the organization has open documents in this report on the as-of date, whatever location the user is signed into and whatever locations they are enrolled in. It is not narrowed by the Location filter, the customer or vendor filter, or the Past due filter; it changes only with the as-of date.
* S5-R4: Each location is named exactly as the location switcher in the top right of ShopView names it, and the Location column uses the same name.
* S5-R5: The filter opens with every location in the list ticked (All locations), so an untouched report shows exactly today's organization-wide rows and totals. "Select all" ticks every location again.
* S5-R6: The chip reads "Location: All locations" when every location is ticked, the location's name when one is ticked (shortened with "..." when long), "Location: N locations" when N are ticked, and "Location: No locations" when none is.
* S5-R6a: With no location ticked ("Clear selection" or unticking every row), the report shows no rows: the native empty state (S8-R5) with "Clear all filters", no totals and no Location column. An export from that state downloads nothing and shows "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results", as on Sales By Customer.
* S5-R7: Choosing locations narrows every row, group, subtotal, total, page count, sort and export to the open documents at those locations. A row belongs to the location of its own document. On A/R: the invoice, credit memo or deposit. On A/P: a bill belongs to the location of the delivery it was received on; a vendor credit from a vendor return belongs to that return's location; any other vendor credit keeps its vendor's location, as today. That is the location the Location column shows.
* S5-R8: On the Summaries, a customer's or vendor's row adds up only their open documents at the chosen locations; a customer or vendor with nothing open there is not listed.
* S5-R9: The chip is shown whenever the report's list (S5-R3) has two or more locations, and always while fewer than all are ticked, so the choice can always be undone.
* S5-R10: The ticked locations are kept in the page address while fewer than all are ticked, so browser Back, a reload and a shared link restore them; a link listing several locations separated by commas is read as those locations. "No locations" is not kept in the address: a reload or shared link opens on All locations, as on Sales By Customer. A link naming every location reads as All locations.
* S5-R10a: Filter choices are not remembered between visits: opening a report from the Reports menu starts on today's as-of date, no customer or vendor, Past due Any, and All locations.
* S5-R11: Clicking a customer or vendor on A/R Summary or A/P Summary opens A/R Collection or A/P Unpaid Invoices with just that customer or vendor ticked, the same as-of date, the same ticked Past due ranges and the same ticked locations.
* S5-R12: The filter does not change who can see what: everyone who can open these reports sees every location's data, as today.
* S5-R13: The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).
* S5-R14: A customer or vendor ticked through a link, a reload or a Summary drill-down is named and ticked on the chip, even when it is not among the first results of the chip's search.
* S5-R15: The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Past due: Any" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the range when one is (for example "Past due: 91+ days"), and "Past due: N ranges" when N are. Ticking all four reads "Past due: 4 ranges", not Any, because Any also keeps invoices and bills that are not due yet. The ranges are the reports' own aging buckets: 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and more than 90 days past the due date on the as-of date.
* S5-R16: With ranges ticked, A/R Detail, A/R Collection, A/P Detail and A/P Unpaid Invoices keep only the invoices and bills whose days past due on the as-of date fall in a ticked range, and always keep credit memos, deposits and vendor credits.

The Detail reports' Amount column holds original amounts and is not compared. With a Past due filter they can differ: a Summary keeps the whole row of a customer or vendor that qualifies (Current and credits included), while a Detail report lists only the invoices or bills that qualify, plus every credit.
* S5-R18b: The figures are read fresh on every load: reloading the report shows a payment recorded a moment before. Going away and back inside the app within 30 seconds, without reloading, can show the figures from the earlier visit, as on every screen.
* S5-R19: The ticked customers or vendors and the ticked Past due ranges are kept in the page address like Location (S5-R10).

* S5-E1: If a location is chosen and the user then picks a customer or vendor with nothing open there, the report is empty and the Location chip stays visible so the selection can be cleared.

- [ ] Given any of the six reports, then the filter row reads, in order, "As of: <date>", "Customer: All customers" (A/R) or "Vendor: All vendors" (A/P, truck icon), "Past due: Any" (grey, hourglass icon) and "Location: All locations" (S5-R1, S5-R13, S5-R15).

- [ ] Given the Customer chip (A/R) or Vendor chip (A/P), then its open menu is exactly Sales By Customer's Customer menu or Inventory Value's Vendor menu (search, shown on the vendor menu only when there are more than 8 vendors, "All customers"/"All vendors", several can be ticked); two ticked read "Customer: 2 customers" and narrow everything to those two (S5-R13).
- [ ] Given the Past due menu, then it shows "Any", "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow.", then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days"; ticking 31-60 and 91+ reads "Past due: 2 ranges"; all four read "Past due: 4 ranges"; none reads grey "Past due: Any" (S5-R15).
- [ ] Given 31-60 and 91+ ticked on a transaction report, then only invoices and bills 31 to 60 or more than 90 days past due remain, plus every credit memo, deposit and vendor credit; on a Summary, only accounts with some invoice or bill amount in those ranges remain, at full balances (S5-R16, S5-R17).
- [ ] Given any combination of filters, then the Totals row adds up exactly the rows left, on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV; on A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices it follows the customer or vendor filter; with Past due on Any, A/R Summary's Totals equal A/R Detail's Open Balance Totals bucket by bucket (and A/P Summary's equal A/P Detail's), and with Past due ranges ticked they can differ as S5-R18a describes; a payment recorded a moment before shows after a reload (S5-R18, S5-R18a, S5-R18b).

- [ ] Given a customer or vendor clicked on a Summary, then Collection or Unpaid Invoices opens with just that one ticked, the same as-of date, Past due ranges and locations, and the chip names it even when it is beyond the search's first page (S5-R11, S5-R14).
- [ ] Given the organization's open documents at only one location and it ticked, then the Location chip is hidden; given a location ticked and then a customer with nothing there, then the report is empty and the chip stays (S5-R9, S5-N1, S5-E1).
- [ ] Given the user switches location in the top right while on a report, then the report reloads with the same filters and rows, the opening sort, collapsed groups and the page at the top (S5-E2).

---

## What changed

Every report has the same four chips: As of, Customer (A/R) or Vendor (A/P), Past due and Location. The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows left. Choices live in the page address, and a Summary name carries them into A/R Collection or A/P Unpaid.

## QA Checklist (do these)

### Filter row \[S5-R1, S5-R13, S5-R15\]

- [ ] Order: As of, Customer (person icon) / Vendor (truck icon), Past due (hourglass), Location. "Customer: All customers" and "Past due: Any" are grey at rest; a choice turns them blue.
- [ ] Customer / Vendor menu: search box, "All customers" / "All vendors", "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." The vendor search box shows only with more than 8 vendors. Two ticked → "Customer: 2 customers".
- [ ] Past due menu: "Any", helper line, "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days". Two ticked → "Past due: 2 ranges"; all four → "Past due: 4 ranges".

### As of \[S3-R4\]

* \[ \] Opens on today at the location. The picker does not offer days after today.
* \[ \] Pick a past date → rows, totals and the Location list are as of the end of that day at the location. In DevTools → Network the requests carry `asOfDate=YYYY-MM-DD` (the picked day).
* \[ \] Edit the address to a later `asOfDate` (e.g. 2027-01-01) → the report opens on today.

### Location \[S5-R2–S5-R10, S5-R6a, S5-N1, S5-E1\]

- [ ] The Location menu lists every location with open documents in this report on the as-of date, whatever location you are signed into, named as in the top-right switcher. "Select all", "N selected", "Clear selection". All ticked → "Location: All locations".
- [ ] Untick one → rows, counts, totals, buckets and exports narrow to documents at the ticked locations. The chip names one location, or reads "N locations".
- [ ] A/P: a bill counts at its delivery's location; a vendor credit from a return at the return's; any other vendor credit at the vendor's.
- [ ] Clear selection → "Location: No locations" (grey): "No record matches these filters" with "Clear all filters", no Totals, no Location column; export → "Empty export".
- [ ] A/R Collection's list leaves out a location whose only open invoices are not yet due (Product confirmed).
- [ ] An organization with one location: no Location chip.

### As of change and ticked locations \[S5-E3\]

- [ ] Setup: 3 locations with open documents today, and an earlier date on which one of them (C) had nothing open.
- [ ] All ticked → change As of to that date → still "Location: All locations".
- [ ] Tick A and C → change As of → only A stays ticked.
- [ ] Tick only C → change As of → back to "Location: All locations".
- [ ] "No locations" → change As of → stays "No locations".
- [ ] If one location is left ticked, the Location column hides and a Location sort falls back to the opening order (SV-11532).

### Past due ranges \[S5-R16, S5-R17, S5-R18\]

* \[ \] Tick 31-60 → only invoices / bills in that range stay, plus **every** credit memo, deposit and vendor credit. The other Detail buckets keep only their credits or read "(0)".
* \[ \] Ranges use calendar days at the location: a document due exactly 31 days before the as-of date is in 31-60.
* \[ \] Summaries with ranges ticked: only customers / vendors with an amount in those ranges remain, at full balances.
* \[ \] The Totals row = the sum of the rows left, on every page and in both exports.

### Summary = Detail \[S5-R18a, S5-R18b\]

- [ ] Past due Any, same As of, customer and locations: A/R Summary Totals = A/R Detail Open Balance Totals, bucket by bucket (Current included). A/P Summary = A/P Detail likewise. Do not compare the Amount column.
- [ ] Record a payment, reload → the new figures show.

### Address and drill-down \[S5-R10, S5-R10a, S5-R11, S5-R14, S5-R19, S5-N2, S5-N3\]

* \[ \] Tick filters, then reload, press Back, or paste the link in a new tab → the same chips come back.
* \[ \] A link with `locationIds=a,b` works; an unknown location id or `pastDue=5` is ignored (All / Any). A deleted customer id next to a valid one → opens with the valid one, no error toast.
* \[ \] A/R Summary: set As of, Past due 31-60 and two locations → click a customer name → A/R Collection opens for that customer (named on the chip) with the same As of, Past due and locations. A/P Summary → A/P Unpaid likewise.
* \[ \] An old bookmark with `?customerId=` / `?vendorId=` still opens filtered to that customer / vendor.
* \[ \] Open A/R Collection from A/R Summary for a customer that is NOT among the first 50 names in the Customer list (e.g. one starting with a late letter) → the Customer chip shows the customer's name, never "Customer: 1 unavailable" (fixed in review round 2, SV-11315 SR-13).
* \[ \] Opening a report from the menu → today, All, Any, All locations.
* \[ \] A location chosen, then a customer with nothing there → empty, Location chip still visible.
* \[ \] Switch location top right while on a report → same filters and rows; sort back to the opening order; groups collapse; back to the top.

### Loading \[S8-R5\]

- [ ] Reload a report on a large organization → the loading bar shows while the filters are read; it never flashes "No record matches these filters" first.

## Known mismatches (not bugs)

* PRD S5-E3 does not mention "No locations"; the build keeps it (Product agreed, wording fix pending).
* **Follow-up:** "today" comes from the browser's time zone data. Between 00:00 and 01:00 Edmonton time, a browser with out-of-date data opens on yesterday and does not offer today in the picker. A picked date is always honoured.
* A location whose record has no organization set shows no name (kept; stricter than the old reports).

## Summary

Give all six reports a column labelled "Location", shown when two or more locations are in scope, so every row says where its document lives.

## Context

As a user of a multi-location shop, I want to see each row's location so that the Location filter has something to match.

Prerequisites: User must have 'Reports → Page Access' setting enabled.

Form factor: Desktop only by rule: detailed reports.

## Requirements

* S6-R1: All six reports have a column labelled exactly "Location". This renames A/R Detail's and A/R Collection's "Location full name" and A/P Detail's and A/P Unpaid Invoices' "Location Name", and adds the column to A/R Summary and A/P Summary.
* S6-R2: The column is shown when two or more locations are ticked (All locations counts when the report's list has two or more) and hidden when one or none is ticked.
* S6-R3: It sits right after the Date column, before the money columns; on A/R Summary and A/P Summary, which have no Date column, right after the customer or vendor name.
* S6-R4: On A/R Summary and A/P Summary a row shows the location's name when all of that customer's or vendor's open documents at the chosen locations are at one location, otherwise "Multiple".
* S6-R5: The column sorts A to Z on its first click; "Multiple" sorts as text.
* S6-N1: With one location chosen, the column is hidden on screen and in the export.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given any of the six reports, then the column is labelled exactly "Location" (replacing "Location full name" and "Location Name"; new on the Summaries) (S6-R1).
- [ ] Given All locations with two or more locations in the report's list, or two or more chosen, then the column shows; given one location chosen, then it is hidden on screen and in the export (S6-R2, S6-N1, S3-R6).
- [ ] Given a detail report, then the column sits right after Date; on the Summaries right after the name (S6-R3).
- [ ] Given a Summary row whose open documents at the chosen locations are at one location, then it shows that location; otherwise "Multiple"; the column sorts A to Z on its first click, "Multiple" as text (S6-R4, S6-R5).

Design: page 4 (Location filter and Location column)

fields.description:
## Summary

Make a document number a link only when the user can open it in its own location, with the existing switch-location prompt for an invoice at another enrolled location; fixes SV-5706.

## Context

As a user, I want a document number to open only when I can actually view it, in its own location, so that I never land on an error.

Prerequisites: An invoice or part sale opens for a user with 'Invoicing & Payments → View' and 'Work Orders → View' (work orders) or 'Part Sales → View' (part sales). A bill opens for a user with 'Vendor Order Management → View' or 'Vendor Order Management → Create & Edit'. A customer name on A/R Summary links to A/R Collection for a user with 'Customers → View', as today. A vendor name on A/P Summary links to A/P Unpaid Invoices for everyone who can open the reports, as today.

Form factor: Desktop only by rule: detailed reports.

## Requirements

* S7-R1: A document number is a link only when the user has the permission to open it and can open it in its own location; otherwise it shows as plain text.
* S7-R2: An invoice or part sale at the user's current location opens its finance page, as today.
* S7-R3: An invoice or part sale at another location the user is enrolled in shows the existing location-switch prompt on the report, before leaving it: title "Switch location?", message "This work order is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?" (for a part sale: "This part sale is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?"), buttons "Cancel" on the left and "Switch location" on the right, and a close × at the top right.
* S7-R4: "Switch location" changes the active location to that location and opens the document.
* S7-R5: "Cancel" or the × closes the prompt; the user stays on the report exactly where they were: same page address, filters, sort, expanded groups and scroll position.
* S7-R6: A bill at the user's current location opens its delivery, as today. A bill at another location shows as plain text, because the bill page cannot switch location.
* S7-R7: Links use the native report link style (the same blue as Work In Progress, semi-bold, no underline, underlined only on keyboard focus), readable in light and dark theme.
* S7-R8: Opening a link in a new tab opens the document page, which asks to switch location itself.
* S7-R9: On A/P Detail and A/P Unpaid Invoices, a vendor credit's number links to the vendor return it came from, under the same rules and permissions as a bill (S7-R6). A vendor credit that did not come from a vendor return shows as plain text.
* S7-R10: A/R credit memos and deposits show as plain text: they have no page of their own.
* S7-N1: A document at a location the user is not enrolled in shows as plain text.
* S7-N2: A document the user lacks the permission for shows as plain text.
* S7-E1: The location switcher in the top right of ShopView is not changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given an invoice or part sale at the user's current location and the permissions in the prerequisites, when its number is clicked, then its finance page opens (S7-R1, S7-R2).
- [ ] Given an invoice at another location the user is enrolled in, when clicked, then the prompt "Switch location?" / "This work order is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?" shows on the report (part sale: "This part sale is in {location}. ..."), with "Cancel" on the left, "Switch location" on the right and a close × at the top right; "Switch location" switches and opens it, and "Cancel" or the × leaves the address, filters, sort, expanded groups and scroll unchanged (S7-R3 to S7-R5).
- [ ] Given a bill at the current location, then it opens its delivery; at another location, plain text; a vendor credit links to the vendor return it came from under the same rules, or is plain text when it came from no return; A/R credit memos and deposits are plain text (S7-R6, S7-R9, S7-R10).
- [ ] Given a document at a location the user is not enrolled in, or without the permission, then it is plain text (S7-N1, S7-N2).
- [ ] Given a link, then it is the native report link style (Work In Progress blue, semi-bold, no underline, underlined on keyboard focus), readable in light and dark; opening it in a new tab opens the document page, which asks to switch location itself (S7-R7, S7-R8).
- [ ] Given a row, when the user clicks anywhere but the link, then nothing opens.

fields.description:
## Summary

Explain each report behind the native info icon beside its title, pin and bold the headline column, fit every column at 1440 pixels, and use the native totals, empty, loading and error states.

## Context

As a user, I want each report to say what it includes and to keep its key total in view so that I understand why totals differ between reports.

Prerequisites: User must have 'Reports → Page Access' setting enabled.

Form factor: Desktop only by rule: detailed reports.

## Requirements

* S8-R1: Each report has the native report info icon (the one Work In Progress and Technician Utilization use) directly right of its title. Hovering, keyboard focus or a tap shows the report's description in a tooltip; moving away or Escape closes it. The descriptions: • A/R Summary: "Each customer’s unpaid balance as of the selected date, after unused credit memos and deposits, with a breakdown of overdue amounts." • A/R Detail: "Each customer’s unpaid invoices, unused credit memos and deposits as of the selected date, grouped by how overdue they are." • A/R Collection: "Overdue invoices, unused credit memos and deposits for each customer to help you follow up on payments. Excludes invoices that aren’t due yet." • A/P Summary: "Your unpaid balance with each vendor as of the selected date, after unused vendor credits, with a breakdown of overdue amounts." • A/P Detail: "Unpaid bills and unused vendor credits as of the selected date, grouped by how overdue they are." • A/P Unpaid Invoices: "Unpaid bills and unused vendor credits grouped by vendor, showing each bill’s due date and days overdue."
* S8-R2: The title, its info icon and the Export menu stay on one line at 1440 pixels wide; the filter row sits below them, positioned as on the native reports.
* S8-R3: The headline column (Open Balance; Total on the Summaries) is pinned to the right edge and bold on the header, every row, every expanded row and the Totals row, as on Sales By Customer. At 1440 pixels wide every column of all six reports is visible without scrolling sideways: the customer or vendor name and Transaction type wrap long values onto a second line, Location wraps only on A/P Detail (nine columns), column headings never wrap, and money, date and number columns never wrap. Narrower than 1440 pixels, the table scrolls sideways under the pinned column.
* S8-R4: The Totals row uses the native totals row style of the newer reports.
* S8-R5: While a report loads it shows the native table progress bar. When the filters leave no rows, it shows the native empty state: "No record matches these filters" and "Try changing filters to widen your results.", with a "Clear all filters" button when a customer or vendor, Past due or Location is chosen; that button keeps the as-of date and returns the customer or vendor, Past due and Location to their defaults (every location ticked).
* S8-R6: If a report fails to load, it shows "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." in place of the rows, with the standard error message.
* S8-N1: The descriptions appear on screen only, not in the PDF or CSV.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given each report, when the user hovers, focuses or taps the info icon right of the title, then its S8-R1 description shows in a tooltip, word for word; moving away or Escape closes it; the descriptions are not in the PDF or CSV (S8-R1, S8-N1).
- [ ] Given a 1440-pixel-wide window, then the title, info icon and ⋯ stay on one line with the filter row below, and every column of all six reports is visible without scrolling sideways, text columns wrapping to a second line, money, date and number columns not wrapping (S8-R2, S8-R3).
- [ ] Given any report, then the headline column (Open Balance; Total on the Summaries) is pinned right and bold on the header, every row, every expanded row and the native Totals row; narrower than 1440 pixels the table scrolls sideways under it (S8-R3, S8-R4).
- [ ] Given filters that leave no rows, then "No record matches these filters" / "Try changing filters to widen your results." shows, with "Clear all filters" when a customer or vendor, Past due or Location is chosen, which keeps the as-of date (S8-R5).
- [ ] Given a load failure, then "Something went wrong loading this report. Please try again." shows in place of the rows, with the standard error message (S8-R6).

## Summary

Show each customer's phone and, for users who manage A/R and A/P data, their credit term on A/R Collection's customer rows and in its exports, so it works as a call list.

## Context

As a user chasing overdue accounts, I want each customer's phone and credit term on A/R Collection so that I can call without opening every customer.

Prerequisites: User must have 'Reports → Page Access' setting enabled.

Form factor: Desktop only by rule: detailed reports.

## Requirements

* S9-R1: On A/R Collection, each customer's group row shows, after the customer's name, "Phone: " and the customer's phone number as the customer card shows it.
* S9-R2: For users with the 'View and Manage AP/AR Data' switch, the group row also shows "Credit term: " and the customer's credit term as the customer card shows it ("COD" when none is set).
* S9-R3: The PDF prints the same phone and credit term on each customer's line; the CSV carries them in columns (S3-R8a).
* S9-N1: A customer with no phone shows no "Phone:" label, on screen or in the PDF.
* S9-N2: A user without 'View and Manage AP/AR Data' sees no credit term on screen, none in the PDF, and no Credit term column in the CSV.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given a customer with a phone, then the customer's group row shows "Phone: <number>" after the name, as the customer card shows it (S9-R1).
- [ ] Given a user with 'View and Manage AP/AR Data', then the row also shows "Credit term: <term>", "COD" when none is set (S9-R2).
- [ ] Given the PDF and CSV, then the PDF prints the same on each customer's line and the CSV carries "Phone" and "Credit term" columns after "Customer" (S9-R3, S3-R8a).
- [ ] Given a customer with no phone, then no "Phone:" label shows on screen or in the PDF (S9-N1).
- [ ] Given a user without 'View and Manage AP/AR Data', then no credit term shows on screen or in the PDF, and the CSV has no Credit term column (S9-N2).
